title: Prakrama 4, Sarga 7. Beholding the Sites of the Stealing of the Garments and Other Pastimes
html:
Krishnadasa leads the Lord through Vrindavana: the fort of carts, the places where Vatsasura, Bakasura, Aghasura, Dhenuka and Pralamba were slain, where Brahma stole the calves, where Kaliya was subdued, the Ghat of the Twelve Adityas, the Bhandira banyan, the Ishika forest where Krishna swallowed the forest fire, the place where He stole the gopis' garments, and where He accepted food from the brahmanas' wives

Verse 1

ततश्च यमुनापारे वृन्दारण्यं सनातनम्।
तत्र नन्दादयो गोपा वासं चक्रुरतन्द्रिताः॥१॥

tataśca yamunāpāre vṛndāraṇyaṁ sanātanam|
tatra nandādayo gopā vāsaṁ cakruratandritāḥ||1||

tatah — then; cha — and; yamuna-pare — across the Yamuna; vrinda-aranyam — Vrindaranya; sanatanam — eternal; tatra — there; nanda-adayah — Nanda and the others; gopah — the cowherds; vasam — dwelling; chakruh — made; atandritah — untiring.

1"And then, across the Yamuna, lies the eternal Vrindaranya; there Nanda and the other cowherds tirelessly made their dwelling.

Verse 2

पश्यात्र शकटैर्दुर्गं कृतं पित्रादिभिर्वृतौ।
रामकृष्णौ खेलतश्च गोगोपालजनैः सह॥२॥

paśyātra śakaṭairdurgaṁ kṛtaṁ pitrādibhirvṛtau|
rāmakṛṣṇau khelataśca gogopālajanaiḥ saha||2||

pashya — behold; atra — here; shakataih — of carts; durgam — the fort; kritam — made; pitri-adibhih — by the fathers and others; vritau — surrounded; rama-krishnau — Rama and Krishna; khelatah — played; cha — and; go-gopala-janaih — with the cows and cowherd folk; saha — together.

2Behold: here the fathers and other elders made a fort of carts; guarded by them, Rama and Krishna played with the cows and the cowherd folk.

Verse 3

कपित्थमूलेऽत्र जनार्दनेन
वधः कृतो वत्सकरूपधारिणः।
वत्सासुरस्य बकवेशधारिणो
बकासुरस्यापि च गौरचन्द्र॥३॥

kapitthamūle'tra janārdanena
vadhaḥ kṛto vatsakarūpadhāriṇaḥ|
vatsāsurasya bakaveśadhāriṇo
bakāsurasyāpi ca gauracandra||3||

kapittha-mule — at the root of the kapittha tree; atra — here; janardanena — by Janardana; vadhah — the slaying; kritah — was done; vatsaka-rupa-dharinah — who took the form of a calf; vatsa-asurasya — of Vatsasura; baka-vesha-dharinah — who took the guise of a crane; baka-asurasya — of Bakasura; api — also; cha — and; gaurachandra — O Gaurachandra.

3Here, at the root of a kapittha tree, Janardana slew Vatsasura, who had taken the form of a calf, and also Bakasura, who came in the guise of a crane, O Gaurachandra1.

Verse 4

अत्रैव श्रीरामजनार्दनौ च
सवेणुवेत्रादियुतैः सखीजनैः।
चिक्रीडतुर्वानरपक्षसङ्कुलै-
र्मयूरकेकादिरुतैर्जगत्पती॥४॥

atraiva śrīrāmajanārdanau ca
saveṇuvetrādiyutaiḥ sakhījanaiḥ|
cikrīḍaturvānarapakṣasaṅkulai-
rmayūrakekādirutairjagatpatī||4||

atra — here; eva — indeed; shri-rama-janardanau — Sri Rama and Janardana; cha — and; sa-venu-vetra-adi-yutaih — carrying flutes, sticks and the like; sakhi-janaih — with their friends; chikridatuh — played; vanara-paksha-sankulaih — amid throngs of monkeys and birds; mayura-keka-adi-rutaih — amid the cries of peacocks and other sounds; jagat-pati — the two Lords of the world.

4Here too Sri Rama and Janardana, the two Lords of the world, played with Their friends, who carried flutes, sticks and the like — amid throngs of monkeys and birds, amid the cries of peacocks and other sounds."

Verse 5

श्रुत्वा स्वयं कृष्णरसेन पूर्णः
श्रीभक्तरूपो रसिकेन्द्रमौलिः।
पूर्वापराभ्यां विषयाश्रयावृतो
लीलारसाभ्यां प्रभुगौरचन्द्रः॥५॥

śrutvā svayaṁ kṛṣṇarasena pūrṇaḥ
śrībhaktarūpo rasikendramauliḥ|
pūrvāparābhyāṁ viṣayāśrayāvṛto
līlārasābhyāṁ prabhugauracandraḥ||5||

shrutva — hearing; svayam — Himself; krishna-rasena — with the rasa of Krishna; purnah — was filled; shri-bhakta-rupah — in the beautiful form of a devotee; rasika-indra-maulih — the crown of the kings of rasikas; purva-aparabhyam — by the former and the present; vishaya-ashraya-avritah — enveloped as both object and abode (of love); lila-rasabhyam — by the rasas of the pastimes; prabhu-gaurachandrah — the Lord Gaurachandra.

5Hearing this, the Lord Gaurachandra — the crown of the kings of rasikas, who had Himself taken the beautiful form of a devotee — was filled with the rasa of Krishna, enfolded by the rasas of both His pastimes, the former and the present, as the object of love and as its abode2.

Verse 6

अत्र पश्य च गौराङ्ग सर्परूपधरोऽप्यघः।
बकानुजो महापापः प्राप्तस्तं चाहनद्धरिः॥६॥

atra paśya ca gaurāṅga sarparūpadharo'pyaghaḥ|
bakānujo mahāpāpaḥ prāptastaṁ cāhanaddhariḥ||6||

atra — here; pashya — behold; cha — and; gauranga — O Gauranga; sarpa-rupa-dharah — taking the form of a serpent; api — also; aghah — Agha; baka-anujah — Baka's younger brother; maha-papah — the great sinner; praptah — came; tam — him; cha — and; ahanat — slew; harih — Hari.

6"Behold here, O Gauranga: here Agha too came in the form of a serpent — Baka's younger brother, a great sinner — and Hari slew him3.

Verse 7

स्वजनैः सखिभिश्चात्र दृष्ट्वा भोजनकौतुकम्।
स्वयम्भूर्वत्सरं वत्सस्वजनापहरोऽभवत्॥७॥

svajanaiḥ sakhibhiścātra dṛṣṭvā bhojanakautukam|
svayambhūrvatsaraṁ vatsasvajanāpaharo'bhavat||7||

svajanaih — with His own; sakhibhih — with His friends; cha — and; atra — here; drishtva — seeing; bhojana-kautukam — the merry feast; svayambhuh — the Self-born (Brahma); vatsaram — for a year; vatsa-svajana-apaharah — the stealer of the calves and His companions; abhavat — became.

7Here the Self-born4, seeing Krishna's merry feast with His kin and friends, stole away the calves and His companions for a year.

Verse 8

धेनुकस्य वधश्चात्र कृपयास्य विमोचनम्।
कालीयदमनं चात्र ह्रदं पश्य सुनिर्मलम्॥८॥

dhenukasya vadhaścātra kṛpayāsya vimocanam|
kālīyadamanaṁ cātra hradaṁ paśya sunirmalam||8||

dhenukasya — of Dhenuka; vadhah — the slaying; cha — and; atra — here; kripaya — by mercy; asya — his; vimochanam — liberation; kaliya-damanam — the subduing of Kaliya; cha — and; atra — here; hradam — the pool; pashya — behold; su-nirmalam — crystal-clear.

8Here Dhenuka was slain and mercifully set free; here Kaliya was subdued5 — behold this crystal-clear pool.

Verse 9

कालीयदमनीं चात्र मूर्तिं पश्य जगद्गुरो।
शीतार्तच्छलतः कृष्ण उत्थितोऽत्र जलाद्बहिः॥९॥

kālīyadamanīṁ cātra mūrtiṁ paśya jagadguro|
śītārtacchalataḥ kṛṣṇa utthito'tra jalādbahiḥ||9||

kaliya-damanim — the subduer of Kaliya; cha — and; atra — here; murtim — the Deity; pashya — behold; jagat-guro — O Teacher of the world; shita-arta-chhalatah — on the pretext of being chilled; krishnah — Krishna; utthitah — rose; atra — here; jalat — from the water; bahih — out.

9Behold here too, O Teacher of the world, the Deity of the Subduer of Kaliya. Here Krishna, pretending to be chilled, came up out of the water.

Verse 10

अत्र वै द्वादशादित्या उत्थिता गगनोपरि।
द्वादशादित्यघट्टोऽयं कथ्यते वेदपारगैः॥१०॥

atra vai dvādaśādityā utthitā gaganopari|
dvādaśādityaghaṭṭo'yaṁ kathyate vedapāragaiḥ||10||

atra — here; vai — indeed; dvadasha-adityah — the twelve Adityas; utthitah — rose; gagana-upari — in the sky; dvadasha-aditya-ghattah — the Ghat of the Twelve Adityas; ayam — this; kathyate — is called; veda-paragaih — by those versed in the Vedas.

10And here the twelve Adityas6 rose in the sky; so those versed in the Vedas call this place the Ghat of the Twelve Adityas.

Verse 11

अत्रैव वत्सपालानां दावाग्नेः परिमोचनम्।
कृतं नन्दकुमारेण भक्तदुःखापहारिणा॥११॥

atraiva vatsapālānāṁ dāvāgneḥ parimocanam|
kṛtaṁ nandakumāreṇa bhaktaduḥkhāpahāriṇā||11||

atra — here; eva — indeed; vatsa-palanam — of the calf-herding boys; dava-agneh — from the forest fire; parimochanam — the deliverance; kritam — was done; nanda-kumarena — by Nanda's son; bhakta-duhkha-apaharina — who takes away His devotees' sorrows.

11Here too Nanda's son, who takes away His devotees' sorrows, delivered the calf-herding boys from the forest fire.

Verse 12

क्रीडापराजितः कृष्णः श्रीदामानाम बालकम्।
उवाह परमप्रीतः प्रलम्बो रोहिणीसुतम्॥१२॥

krīḍāparājitaḥ kṛṣṇaḥ śrīdāmānāma bālakam|
uvāha paramaprītaḥ pralambo rohiṇīsutam||12||

krida-parajitah — defeated in the game; krishnah — Krishna; shridama nama — named Shridama; balakam — the boy; uvaha — carried; parama-pritah — most gladly; pralambah — Pralamba; rohini-sutam — the son of Rohini.

12Having lost a game, Krishna gladly carried a boy named Shridama, while Pralamba carried the son of Rohini7.

Verse 13

ज्ञात्वासुरं पुनः सोऽपि मुष्टीकृत्य कराम्बुजम्।
शिरस्यताडयत्तस्य सोऽपतद्गतजीवितः॥१३॥

jñātvāsuraṁ punaḥ so'pi muṣṭīkṛtya karāmbujam|
śirasyatāḍayattasya so'patadgatajīvitaḥ||13||

jnatva — recognising; asuram — the demon; punah — then; sah — He; api — indeed; mushtikritya — clenching into a fist; kara-ambujam — His lotus hand; shirasi — on the head; atadayat — struck; tasya — his; sah — he; apatat — fell; gata-jivitah — lifeless.

13But He saw through the demon, clenched His lotus hand into a fist and struck him on the head, and the demon fell down lifeless.

Verse 14

भाण्डीराख्यं वटं वृन्दारण्ये पश्य महत्तमम्।
ईषिकाख्यवनं ह्यत्र गोधनं तृणलोभितम्॥१४॥

bhāṇḍīrākhyaṁ vaṭaṁ vṛndāraṇye paśya mahattamam|
īṣikākhyavanaṁ hyatra godhanaṁ tṛṇalobhitam||14||

bhandira-akhyam — called Bhandira; vatam — the banyan; vrinda-aranye — in Vrindaranya; pashya — behold; mahattamam — the greatest; ishika-akhya-vanam — the forest called Ishika; hi — indeed; atra — here; go-dhanam — the herd; trina-lobhitam — lured by the grass.

14Behold the greatest banyan in Vrindaranya, called Bhandira. And here is the forest called Ishika. The herd, lured by the grass,

Verse 15

प्रविष्टं वेणुनादेन कृष्णेनानीतमप्युत।
दावानले मध्यगं च स्वगणं वीक्ष्य श्रीहरिः॥१५॥

praviṣṭaṁ veṇunādena kṛṣṇenānītamapyuta|
dāvānale madhyagaṁ ca svagaṇaṁ vīkṣya śrīhariḥ||15||

pravishtam — that had entered; venu-nadena — by the sound of the flute; krishnena — by Krishna; anitam — brought back; api uta — and also; dava-anale — in the forest fire; madhya-gam — caught in the midst; cha — and; sva-ganam — His own people; vikshya — seeing; shri-harih — Sri Hari.

15wandered into it, and Krishna brought it back with the sound of His flute. And when Sri Hari saw His companions caught in the midst of the forest fire,

Verse 16

पपौ करतलीकृत्यानलं भक्तजनप्रियः।
पश्य चात्र रसज्ञेन श्रीकृष्णेन कृतं हि यत्॥१६॥

papau karatalīkṛtyānalaṁ bhaktajanapriyaḥ|
paśya cātra rasajñena śrīkṛṣṇena kṛtaṁ hi yat||16||

papau — drank; karatali-kritya — taking into His palm; analam — the fire; bhakta-jana-priyah — who loves His devotees; pashya — behold; cha — and; atra — here; rasa-jnena — by the knower of rasa; shri-krishnena — by Sri Krishna; kritam — was done; hi — indeed; yat — what.

16He who loves His devotees took the fire into His palm and drank it8. Behold too what Sri Krishna, the knower of rasa, did here.

Verse 17

तमेव पतिमिच्छन्त्यो व्रतं चेरुः कुमारिकाः।
अत्रैव यमुनातीरे वस्त्राभरणरक्षिताः॥१७॥

tameva patimicchantyo vrataṁ ceruḥ kumārikāḥ|
atraiva yamunātīre vastrābharaṇarakṣitāḥ||17||

tam — Him; eva — alone; patim — as husband; ichchhantyah — desiring; vratam — a vow; cheruh — observed; kumarikah — the maidens; atra — here; eva — indeed; yamuna-tire — on the bank of the Yamuna; vastra-abharana-rakshitah — having laid aside their clothes and ornaments.

17Desiring Him alone as their husband, the maidens kept a vow9. Here, on the bank of the Yamuna, they laid aside their clothes and ornaments

Verse 18

विशन्त्यो जलमेवैतास्ततो नागरशेखरः।
आदाय तासां वस्त्राणि नीपमारुह्य सत्वरः॥१८॥

viśantyo jalamevaitāstato nāgaraśekharaḥ|
ādāya tāsāṁ vastrāṇi nīpamāruhya satvaraḥ||18||

vishantyah — entering; jalam — the water; eva — indeed; etah — they; tatah — then; nagara-shekharah — the crest-jewel of refined lovers (nagaras); adaya — taking; tasam — their; vastrani — clothes; nipam — a nipa tree; aruhya — climbing; satvarah — swiftly.

18and went into the water. Then the crest-jewel of lovers took their clothes and nimbly climbed a nipa tree10.

Verse 19

हसति शाखिभिः सार्धं ततस्ताः शीतवेपिताः।
कृष्णं सन्तोषयामासुः शुद्धभावेन भाविताः॥१९॥

hasati śākhibhiḥ sārdhaṁ tatastāḥ śītavepitāḥ|
kṛṣṇaṁ santoṣayāmāsuḥ śuddhabhāvena bhāvitāḥ||19||

hasati — laughs; shakhibhih — the trees; sardham — together with; tatah — then; tah — they; shita-vepitah — shivering with cold; krishnam — Krishna; santoshayam asuh — satisfied; shuddha-bhavena — with pure feeling; bhavitah — imbued.

19He laughs — and the trees laugh with Him. And they, shivering with cold and imbued with pure feeling, satisfied Krishna.

Verse 20

श्रीरामेण समं कृष्णस्तमुद्दिश्य वनस्पतीन्।
वृन्दारण्यस्थितानत्र प्रशंसन् यमुनां गतः॥२०॥

śrīrāmeṇa samaṁ kṛṣṇastamuddiśya vanaspatīn|
vṛndāraṇyasthitānatra praśaṁsan yamunāṁ gataḥ||20||

shri-ramena — with Sri Rama; samam — together; krishnah — Krishna; tam — to him; uddishya — pointing out; vanaspatin — the trees; vrinda-aranya-sthitan — standing in Vrindaranya; atra — here; prashamsan — praising; yamunam — to the Yamuna; gatah — went.

20Here Krishna, together with Sri Rama, pointing out to Him the trees of Vrindaranya and praising them, went on to the Yamuna.

Verse 21

ततोऽत्र विप्रपत्नीभ्यश्चान्नमादाय यज्ञभुक्।
बुभुजे बालकैः सार्धं बलेनापि बलीयसा॥२१॥

tato'tra viprapatnībhyaścānnamādāya yajñabhuk|
bubhuje bālakaiḥ sārdhaṁ balenāpi balīyasā||21||

tatah — then; atra — here; vipra-patnibhyah — from the brahmanas' wives; cha — and; annam — the food; adaya — accepting; yajna-bhuk — the Enjoyer of sacrifices; bubhuje — ate; balakaih — with the boys; sardham — together; balena — with Bala; api — and; baliyasa — the mighty.

21And then, here, the Enjoyer of sacrifices accepted food from the brahmanas' wives11 and ate it with the boys and with mighty Bala."

Thus ends the seventh sarga, "Beholding the Sites of the Stealing of the Garments and Other Pastimes" (Vastra-harana-adi-lila-sthali-darshana), of the fourth prakrama of the poem "Sri Krishna-chaitanya-charitamrita."

✦

Notes

  1. Vatsasura and Bakasura: demons sent by Kamsa, who took the forms of a calf and of a huge crane (Bhagavata Purana 10.11).
  2. Vishaya is the object of love (Krishna), ashraya its abode (the devotee). In His former pastime the Lord, as Krishna, was the object of love; in the present one, as Gaura, He is its abode.
  3. Aghasura swallowed the cowherd boys and calves in the form of a huge serpent and was slain by Krishna from within (Bhagavata Purana 10.12).
  4. The Self-born (Svayambhu): Brahma (Bhagavata Purana 10.13).
  5. Dhenuka: the ass-demon slain by Balarama; Kaliya: the many-headed serpent who poisoned the Yamuna and whom Krishna subdued by dancing on his heads (Bhagavata Purana 10.15–16).
  6. The Adityas: the twelve sons of Aditi, solar deities; according to local tradition, they rose to warm Krishna as He came out of Kaliya's pool.
  7. Shridama: a friend of Krishna; the son of Rohini: Balarama. The demon Pralamba, who had slipped into the cowherd boys' game, tried to carry Balarama off (Bhagavata Purana 10.18).
  8. Bhagavata Purana 10.17 and 10.19.
  9. The vow to the goddess Katyayani, which the gopis kept to obtain Krishna as their husband (Bhagavata Purana 10.22). Their desire is pure prema, not worldly passion: as Krishna Himself says, desire directed to Him bears no worldly fruit, just as roasted grain does not sprout (ibid. 10.22.26).
  10. Nipa: the kadamba tree.
  11. Bhagavata Purana 10.23.
